newsitem.title: USA: Calif. fund withdraws Rollins board proposal.
newsitem.headline: Calif. fund withdraws Rollins board proposal.

text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said Friday it withdrew its shareholder proposal that called for Rollins Environmental Services Inc to restructure its board of directors to include a majority of independent directors.
CalPERS said it withdrew the proposal because of the recent proposed merger between Rollins Environmental Services and Laidlaw Inc.
"We are gratified to see additional independent directors included as part of the marriage between these two companies," Kayla Gillan, CalPERS general counsel, said.
"This action indicates that Rollins has seriously considered the benefits of independent directors and is one step closer to improving the value of investments for all shareholders," Gillan said.

The new company's board would have 10 directors, consisting of three members appointed by Rollins Environmental Services, four members appointed by Laidlaw, and three independent directors chosen jointly by both companies.

"This merger saves Rollins from financial ruin," said Gillan. "We are optimistic that the new company will be better equipped to survive in the declining hazardous waste industry and we will certainly continue to monitor its performance."

CalPERS filed its proposal in August 1996 urging the Rollins Environmental Services board of directors to take steps to amend the company's bylaws to require that a majority of the board be made up of independent directors.
CalPERS is the nation's largest public pension fund. It provides retirement and health benefits to one million active and retired public employees and their families.
